title: Implement the documented high-water-mark system (bronze_load_metadata + parameter flow) — or formally descope it via /iterate
description: incremental_load_strategy.md sections 4-5 specify a bronze_load_metadata table, get_last_load_date()/update_load_metadata() functions, and p_from_date flowing to the bronze dataflows. NONE of it exists: grep across fabric/ and src/ finds no bronze_load_metadata anywhere; the pipeline passes a static p_from_date defaulting to '1900-01-01' (pipeline-content.json:478-481); and the bronze dataflow activities receive no parameters at all (bronze_procurement activity, lines 290-307). Net effect today: 'incremental' mode reprocesses all of bronze from 1899-12-25 through the fragile MERGE path (see task-024) with none of the documented 70-90% savings, and bronze always full-loads regardless. This is the largest single doc-vs-implementation drift in the incremental strategy. Two honest resolutions: (a) implement the watermark (metadata table + notebook auto-retrieve + optionally dataflow parameter pushdown), or (b) decide the portfolio project doesn't need real watermarking and update the strategy doc to describe the actual design (static parameter, caller-supplied watermark) via /iterate.
acceptanceCriteria: Path chosen and recorded: (a) implement watermark, or (b) descope with doc update via /iterate. If (b), the remaining criteria below are replaced by the doc reconciliation and this task closes with the /iterate proposal applied.
If (a): bronze_load_metadata Delta table created per incremental_load_strategy.md:399-421 schema (source_table, last_load_date, load_timestamp, rows_loaded, load_status, execution_id).

If (a): bronze-to-silver resolves the effective watermark per the doc's precedence (full_load -> 1900-01-01; explicit p_from_date override; else auto-retrieve last SUCCESS from metadata — doc lines 576-599), and writes a metadata row after load (SUCCESS with max date loaded / FAILED on exception, doc lines 449-474).
If (a): silver-to-gold consumes the same effective watermark for its filtered read (coordinates with task-024's gold-side p_from_date filter — same watermark value, don't invent a second mechanism).

If (a): [Erik/Fabric] two consecutive incremental runs demonstrate the watermark advancing (second run reads only the look-back window) and a forced failure leaves a FAILED row without advancing the watermark.

Dataflow-side pushdown (p_from_date into bronze_procurement dataflow, doc section 5) is explicitly decided: implemented, or deferred with a note in the doc — bronze full-refresh may be acceptable at demo volume, but the doc must stop claiming otherwise.
notes: [IMPLEMENTED 2026-07-28] Path (a) built. src/transformations/watermark.py (reference impl: resolve_effective_watermark, metadata_row, get_last_load_date, update_load_metadata). bronze-to-silver notebook: inline mirror of all four + effective_from_date resolution + p_execution_id param + try/except around procurement write writing SUCCESS (max date loaded) or FAILED (effective_from_date attempted) metadata rows; empty-window (None max date) skips the SUCCESS row. silver-to-gold2 notebook: inline mirror of read-side functions + effective_from_date via get_last_load_date(exclude_execution_id=p_execution_id) for gold coordination; fact_procurement read keys off effective_from_date. pipeline-content.json: added p_execution_id parameter (default '') + @pipeline().RunId binding to both notebook activities. incremental_load_strategy.md §4-5 rewritten to describe shipped design (auto-retrieve sentinel, source_table naming, gold coordination via exclude_execution_id, bronze full-refresh deferred per criterion 6). tests/test_watermark.py: 27 tests (precedence, row construction, read path over Spark fixture, notebook parity for both notebooks). tests/conftest.py: added spark.sql.ansi.enabled=false. Precedence: full_load→1900-01-01; explicit p_from_date!=1900-01-01→override; else auto-retrieve last SUCCESS. Source_table: single key 'bronze_procurement_transactional' shared by silver+gold. Gold coordination: gold excludes the current run's execution_id so it reads the PREVIOUS run's watermark (one mechanism, one value per run) — recorded as DEC-006. Pipeline touched: YES — p_execution_id added (justified: gold coordination needs a pipeline-level run identifier so silver-to-gold2 can distinguish the current run's just-written SUCCESS row from the previous run's).
AUDIT-DERIVED (pipeline quality audit 2026-07-13): finding #10 (high tier). Not spec-decomposed — empty drift fingerprints.

EVIDENCE: Grep for bronze_load_metadata/get_last_load_date across fabric/ and src/ returns nothing (only the local 'watermark_date' variable in bronze-to-silver:180). Pipeline parameter defaults at pipeline-content.json:474-481. Bronze dataflow activities carry no parameters: bronze_procurement at lines 290-307, bronze_WGI at 272-289, bronze_EPI at 308-325. Doc contract: incremental_load_strategy.md sections 4 (lines 397-474) and 5 (lines 478-599).
DEPENDS ON task-024 because the value of a watermark is moot until the MERGE path it feeds is safe, and 024 may add the the gold-side p_from_date filter this task then wires to the metadata table.
FILE CONFLICT: pipeline-content.json is also touched by task-022 (In Progress) and task-026 — serialize.

DESCOPE GUIDANCE: if (b), the doc rewrite goes through /iterate per DEC-016 only if the content lives in spec files; incremental_load_strategy.md is a support document, so a direct edit is permitted — but check whether spec_v1.md references the watermark design (grep 'watermark|high-water' in .claude/spec_v1.md first; if yes, that part routes through /iterate).

test_protocol.summary: Erik's Fabric-side two-run watermark advancement + forced-failure test (criterion 5). Delta ops cannot run locally (delta-spark not installed) — this protocol exercises the end-to-end watermark system in Fabric.

steps.instruction: Sync the pipeline-content.json change (p_execution_id parameter + @pipeline().RunId binding) and notebook changes to Fabric via /sync-to-fabric. Confirm the p_execution_id parameter appears in the orchestrator pipeline's parameter list.
steps.expected: Pipeline artifact in Fabric shows p_execution_id parameter (default empty string) and both notebook activities (bronze-to-silver, silver-to-gold) receive p_execution_id bound to @pipeline().RunId.

steps.instruction: Run 1 (initial): Trigger orchestrator_pipeline_bronze_to_gold with p_full_load=false, p_from_date=1900-01-01 (sentinel). Observe notebook stdout in the activity logs.
steps.expected: bronze-to-silver stdout shows '[watermark] p_full_load='false' p_from_date='1900-01-01' last_SUCCESS=None execution_id='<run-id>' -> effective_from_date='1900-01-01'' (no prior SUCCESS row). After run, query: SELECT * FROM oem_lh.bronze_load_metadata WHERE source_table='bronze_procurement_transactional' ORDER BY load_timestamp DESC LIMIT 3 — expect at least 1 SUCCESS row with last_load_date = max(Date) from bronze_procurement_transactional, load_status='SUCCESS', execution_id populated with the pipeline RunId.

steps.instruction: Run 2 (incremental): Trigger the pipeline again with the same parameters. Observe notebook stdout.
steps.expected: bronze-to-silver stdout shows '[watermark] ... last_SUCCESS=<date-from-run-1> ... -> effective_from_date='<YYYY-MM-DD>'' where YYYY-MM-DD is the previous run's max date (NOT 1900-01-01). silver-to-gold2 stdout shows the SAME effective_from_date (gold coordination via exclude_execution_id — gold excludes the current RunId and reads the previous SUCCESS). The silver read window is the 7-day look-back from effective_from_date, NOT the full table. A new SUCCESS row is appended to bronze_load_metadata with the new max date.

steps.instruction: Forced failure: Force the procurement write to fail — e.g., drop oem_lh.silver_procurement before the write step, or inject a schema mismatch. Trigger the pipeline.
steps.expected: bronze-to-silver stdout shows '[watermark] FAILED row written — attempted_from=<effective_from_date> execution_id='<run-id>' error=...'. The activity fails (exception re-raised). Query bronze_load_metadata: expect a FAILED row with last_load_date = effective_from_date attempted, rows_loaded=0, load_status='FAILED'. The previous SUCCESS row is UNCHANGED — watermark did NOT advance.

steps.instruction: Recovery run: Fix the failure condition (recreate silver_procurement or restore schema). Trigger the pipeline again with the same parameters.
steps.expected: bronze-to-silver auto-retrieves the PREVIOUS SUCCESS watermark (the FAILED row is filtered out by load_status='SUCCESS'). The effective_from_date is the last SUCCESS date, not the FAILED row's attempted date — confirming the watermark did not advance on failure and the system recovers correctly.
